name: News Brief
summary: An evidence board in which every claim carries its state: confirmed claims are solid and stamped, unconfirmed ones are dashed and grey. One reusable object (map, tile grid, timeline) changes state across the film.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Say what happened, what is confirmed, what is not, and what to watch next.
visual_job.hero: A map, tile grid or timeline with a visible confidence state per claim.

use_when: An event is recent or still developing.
Sources disagree or part of the story is unconfirmed.
The film is short-form and portrait.
avoid_when: The event is settled history (use chronicle).
The story is a feeling rather than a set of claims (use storybook).

alternates.when: Illustrated treatment, as in the Korea and cloud films.

scene_grammar.formula: What, where, when stamped in the first second, with the hero object already on screen.
Confirmed facts one at a time, each with a source chip.
Map pins or dated ticks on a timeline.
How big: a counter or a one-cell-one-unit grid whose state changes.
What is not confirmed, drawn differently from what is: dashed, grey, labelled.
What officials or companies did, as dated steps.
The open questions and what to watch.
Sources and the 'as of' date; the picture still moves.

motion.signature: Evidence appears with its state, and one reusable object changes state across the film.
motion.continuous_layer: A drift layer on the hero object plus a second moving layer (counter, travelling dot, label sweep) so the whole frame changes.
avoid: Confirmed and unconfirmed claims drawn the same way.

rules.ending: Land a soft thud and ring on the last visual event; hold the bed; tail after the last word 2-3 s.

short_form.closing: Reel-length films (60 s or less): close on a word or image from the hook so a replay lands clean, then keep the soft thud and the tail above.

anti_patterns.pattern: Narration over a frame that does not change for more than max_beat_gap_sec.
anti_patterns.why: Breaks the anti-laziness rule. motion-qa flagged 41 s of 70 (cloud), 44 s of 92 (fridge), 79 s of 98 (Korea) as static or low-energy. Plan one visual event per 2-3 s from measured onsets and give every scene a drift layer (Studio.space.drift).

anti_patterns.pattern: A hero grid or map where only a few cells change per beat.
anti_patterns.why: The detector reads the whole frame: Korea's tile grid changed 4-11% of the frame and was flagged idle. Add a second moving layer (counter, travelling dot, label sweep).

anti_patterns.pattern: Labels below the type floor (2.6% of the short side) to fit more on screen.
anti_patterns.why: Cloud had 21 text-size-floor warnings at 12.5-17 px and still shipped at readability 3. Cut the label or split the beat; never shrink the type.

anti_patterns.pattern: Leader lines or tags that touch other text or sit on their own node.
anti_patterns.why: Fridge's dotted leader ran through 'ONLINE'; cloud's 'DELHI' tag sat on its node; a phone touched a kicker. No check catches this; open the full-size frame at each scene's first and last beat.

anti_patterns.pattern: A headline that restates the narration.
anti_patterns.why: Fridge headlines repeated 82-83% of the voice, which wastes the strongest text slot. Use it for what the voice does not say (the number, the contrast, the date). A caption band is a legitimate repeat.

anti_patterns.pattern: The same empty stage in most scenes.
anti_patterns.why: repeat-layout-dom fired in all three films (3-5 of 6 scenes). A recurring grid is fine when its state changes; vary the hero's position or scale between scenes.

anti_patterns.pattern: Over-budget narration in the hook and closing scenes.
anti_patterns.why: They are written last. Cloud's s1 and s6 ran 35-36 words per 10 s against a 33 budget and the film read rushed. Cut words; do not raise the speed.

anti_patterns.pattern: Ramping the bed to zero over the last seconds.
anti_patterns.why: Cloud's last moment measured 19 LU under the body. Land a soft thud and ring on the last visual event, hold the bed, keep the tail after the last word to 2-3 s.
Korea opened on 0.33 s of empty frame (flat-frame warning). Start the hero already drawn or fading in from frame 1.

anti_patterns.pattern: A greeting, a title card or a framing sentence before the claim.
anti_patterns.why: The film starts at the sentence you would normally reach at second six. No welcome, no 'in this video', no logo sting. A stamped event opens on the date and the fact.
anti_patterns.source: ig-reel rules (Jake Schincariol, MIT), adopted 2026-11-05 via docs/short-form-lessons.md.

anti_patterns.pattern: More than one ask at the end.
anti_patterns.why: End on one action or none. Two asks split the last three seconds and the viewer does neither. A news brief usually needs none.
anti_patterns.source: ig-reel rules (Jake Schincariol, MIT), adopted 2026-11-05 via docs/short-form-lessons.md; checked by `studio.py script` (many-asks).

anti_patterns.pattern: A hook sentence longer than the three-second window.
anti_patterns.why: south-korea-data-center-fire opens on one 9.8 s sentence (date, place, event and agency together). Say the claim first and move the detail to the next sentence.

reference_projects.note: Best audio, calmest pace; one 647-tile grid reused for burn and recovery.
Phone and cloud bookend; most label and layout problems.
Tile grid that heats and returns cooled; diegetic compressor bed.

open_questions: motion-qa does not yet waive low-contrast and text-echo for a declared caption band (TODO.md).
No rule for how stale a 'latest' figure may be before it needs an 'as of' date on screen.

revisions.change: Initial version. Built from the 2026-11-03 review of the three newest films: most anti-patterns and the 2.0 s beat gap come from it.
Added rules.short_form (cards of 6 words or fewer, loop ending for reel-length films) and three anti-patterns: framing sentence before the claim, more than one ask, hook longer than 3 s.
revisions.reason: docs/short-form-lessons.md; the card limit is measured against the three newest films (cloud 2 of 35 cards over 6 words, fridge 3 of 27, Korea 9 of 51).
